name: Cailleach Uragaig

facts.text: Level 70, 10,000 health, crowd-control immune, armour factor 350 with 20% absorb, 20% resist to everything. Drawn past her tether she takes no damage from any attacker (players, pets and bots alike).

When she engages she cries 'Father! Lend me your Torch of Light so we may be delivered from these aggressors!' and four Mithra's Torches of Light (level 65, untargetable, flying, no name) appear at four fixed places round her pillars; each throws Flame Spear (150 heat, instant, range 4,000) at her target, and all four are removed five seconds after she engages.

She casts Flame Spear herself: a 200 heat bolt, 4 s cast, range 1,800, not marked uninterruptible. Below 30% her script calls helpers with the package CailleachUragaigBaf within 2,500; no world spawn carries that package, so nobody answers. Out of combat she walks home at full health.
Seven cailleach priests and seven cailleach guards (levels 60-67) stand round her pillars as their own camp.

facts.text: Mithraic mysteries, not game canon: the highest grade of initiate was Pater, 'Father', and the torchbearers Cautes and Cautopates carried torches raised and lowered.
Gaelic folklore, not game canon: the Cailleach is the hag of winter. Uragaig is a place name on Colonsay (to verify).

story:
The Cailleach is the old woman of the cold in the tales of the north, who carries winter in her apron and strikes the ground with her staff to harden it. The Cornish say one came south in the year Lyonesse drowned, because the drowned country was cold and wet enough to suit her, and because there was a house standing empty there that had been built for a god.

The house was Rome's. West of the road, inside a ring of pillars, the soldiers of the legions had kept their god Mithras, the bull-slayer born from the rock, and his priests were known by their grades from Raven up to Father, and two of them carried torches at his side, one raised and one lowered. When Rome went home the god stayed, as gods do, with nobody left to call him by his name. The Cailleach called him. Whether she was a priestess of that cult who grew old past dying, or a hag of the north who found a god asleep and woke him for her own use, the fishermen below the pillars will not say. They say she calls him Father, and that he answers.

He answers once. When the sisterhood's house is threatened she cries out to him, and the torches of the god stand up in the air round the pillars, four of them, burning with no flame you could warm your hands at, and all of them throw at the one she has marked, together, and then go dark. 'The Father lends his torches,' the Danaoin fishermen say when a thing is given and taken back in the same breath; 'he does not give them.' After that she is alone with her own fire, and she makes it the slow way, a spear of it at a time, drawing each one up out of the cold ground while she mutters; the fishermen say a shout in her ear at the wrong moment and the spear falls to nothing in her hand.

Her sisters keep the ring with her: old women in grey who were once, perhaps, the girls of the drowned villages, and the guards who stand at the pillars' feet. The sisterhood is not her bodyguard. It is her household, and keeps its own counsel, and has its own quarrel with anyone who walks in among the pillars uninvited. Lidmann Halsey of Adribard's Retreat sends the realm's Defenders to her because she has been drawing the cold of the north down into Albion's west for a long time, and the Cornish cannot get their harvests in. She cannot be hurt off her own ground; the house of the god keeps her. On it she is an old woman with a god's borrowed fire, and the Cornish will not say her name.
legend: The Cailleach Uragaig, level 70, 10k, in the ring of pillars straight west off the Lyonesse road. Her sisterhood is around her: seven priests and seven guards, 60s, their own camp, so clear the ones close to her first or fight her where they will not join. When she aggroes, four torches of Mithra appear round the pillars and each throws a 150 heat bolt at her target, then they vanish five seconds later. You cannot target the torches and you do not need to: have the first target topped and heat resist up. After that she casts a 200 heat bolt with a 4 second cast, so interrupt her. She is crowd-control immune and takes no damage if you drag her off her pillars. Her old 30% call for help finds nobody in this world. About half an hour respawn.

loremasterTopic.text: The hag of the cold, from the tales of the north, who keeps house in Rome's ring of pillars in [lyonesse] with her sisterhood. She calls the old god Mithras Father, and his torches answer her once and go out; after that her fire comes the slow way. The house keeps her: off her own ground nothing bites. The Cornish will not say her name.

bookPage: From the letters of Clemo Penrose, sexton of the broken cathedral. Of the pillars west of the road. A company of Defenders went in among them in the spring, past the old women in grey, and I watched from the fishermen's huts. The hag cried out to her Father and four torches stood up in the air round the pillars, and every one of them threw at the same knight, who went down on one knee and got up again because a priest was already at his shoulder, and then the torches were gone. After that it was the hag's own fire, slow to make. Every time she drew a spear up out of the ground a little minstrel sang at her, very loud and very badly, and the spear went to nothing in her hand. I think he saved them all.
